newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli shekel gains against dollar.
newsitem.headline: Israeli shekel gains against dollar.

text.p: The Israeli shekel representative rate was fixed higher against the dollar on Wednesday in dull trading after the U.S. currency fell off its highs in Europe, dealers said.

"Trading was very quiet today. The basket traded slightly above seven percent (floor) under the diagonal rate and the Bank of Israel was not seen in the market," said a dealer at Israel Discount Bank.
"The shekel recovered slightly against the dollar after the U.S. currency declined against the mark in Europe," he added.

The shekel is allowed to fluctuate in a trading band of seven percent above or below a sloping mid-point designed to devalue the Israeli currency at a rate of six percent a year against the basket of key currencies.

The representative rate for the dollar was fixed at 3.3520 shekels against 3.3590 on Tuesday. The basket, composed of the dollar, mark, pound sterling, French franc and yen, was fixed at 3.6384 shekels against 3.6378 on Tuesday.
On the crosses the shekel traded against the yen at 2.7058 shekels per 100 yen against 2.7042 on Tuesday and against the mark at 1.9806 shekels against 1.9734 on Tuesday.
In late afternoon the dollar was trading at 3.3520 shekels.
